images.caption:
Inscription reads:
STANDING ROCK
INYAN WOSLATA
A famous sacred stone which many years ago came into possession of the Sioux. According to Dakota legend, it is a body of a young Indian woman with her child on her back who were [sic] left in camp she refused to accompany the tribe as they moved south. When others were sent back to find her, she was found to have turned to stone. The stone is held in reverence by the Sioux and it is placed here overlooking the waters and the empire once held by the mighty Sioux Nation.
Sponsored By
Local Lions Club
American Legion

Tribal Council 1963

images.filename: Native American Scenic Byway - Sitting Bull Monument - NARA - 7720608.jpg
images.caption:
Scope and content:  The original finding aid described this photograph as:
Original Caption: The Standing Rock Native American Scenic Byway takes you past two places where one of the greatest leaders in American history is said to be buried. Sitting Bull died along the Grand River in western Standing Rock December 15, 1890 and was subsequently buried at Fort Yates, North Dakota. This site is marked and located on the drive into Fort Yates, within one mile of the Standing Rock Native American Scenic Byway. Later, Sitting Bull's remains were said to have been removed to a site across from Mobridge, South Dakota marked by a stone monument carved by famed sculptor Korczak Ziolkowski, located south of Grand River Casino, three miles off the byway.
Location: Fort Yates, North Dakota (46.088° N 100.629° W)

Status: Public domain.

images.filename: The original burial site of Sitting Bull at Ft. Yates, ND.jpg
images.caption: The City of Mobridge, ND wanted to disinter the bones of Sitting Bull from his original burial site and relocate them to a site in Mobridge as a tourist attraction.  The descendants of Sitting Bull were convinced to do this, and a after a lengthy court battle, they won the right to remove the bones.  Ft. Yates still maintains the original burial site, though it is rather poorly maintained and not well marked for tourists.
